e-8604.knowledge_point: Finding the Matrix of a Linear Map Relative to Two Bases Using the Definition
e-8604.problem:
Suppose $\mathbf{T} : V \rightarrow W$ is a linear map and $\mathcal{B}=\{ \mathbf{b}_1,\mathbf{b}_2, \mathbf{b}_3 \}$ and $\mathcal{C} = \{ \mathbf{c}_1,\mathbf{c}_2 \}$ are the bases of the vector spaces $V$ and $W,$ respectively. Find the matrix $[\mathbf{T}]_{\mathcal{B}|\mathcal{C}}$ of the map $\mathbf{T}$ relative to these bases, if 

$\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{b}_1)=-3\mathbf{c}_1+5\mathbf{c}_2,\quad$ $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{b}_2)=\mathbf{c}_2-2\mathbf{c}_1\quad$ and $\quad\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{b}_3)=\mathbf{c}_1+5\mathbf{c}_2.$
e-8604.worked_solution:
First, we write the images of vectors in $\mathcal{B}$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{C} \mathbin{:}$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}T({b}_{1})=-3{c}_{1}+5{c}_{2} & \,⟹\,[T({b}_{1})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\ T({b}_{2})={c}_{2}-2{c}_{1} & \,⟹\,[T({b}_{2})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T({b}_{3})={c}_{1}+5{c}_{2} & \,⟹\,[T({b}_{3})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, $[\mathbf{T}]_{\mathcal{B}|\mathcal{C}}$ is the matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{b}_1),$ $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{b}_2)$ and $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{b}_3)$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{C}\mathbin{:}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14067114/assets/215cd69925ccfeab3ccb20874b7cdc2d837b99f33d8112f95fa5d2b646a27d40.png)

e-8605.knowledge_point: Finding the Matrix of a Linear Map Relative to Two Bases Given One Basis
e-8605.problem:
Consider the basis $\mathcal{B}=\{\mathbf{b}_1, \mathbf{b}_2, \mathbf{b}_3\}$ of the vector space $V$ and the basis $\mathcal{C}$ of $\mathbb{R}^2$ given by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14067114/assets/7c123e6f7d842a8e86e4c99826d25df070982514960752a25481a9f3f046cc1b.png)

Find the matrix $[\mathbf{T}]_{\mathcal{B}|\mathcal{C}}$ of the map $\mathbf{T}:V \to \mathbb{R}^2$ relative to these bases if 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14067114/assets/9a469219c661453d7891935b2ef0a32bff972bcf903d641ca7e31b7bec26369a.png)
e-8605.worked_solution:
Recall that $[\mathbf{T}]_{\mathcal{B}|\mathcal{C}}$ is the matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{b}_1),$ $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{b}_2),$ and $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{b}_3)$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{C}.$

First, we need to find the coordinates of $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{b}_i)$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{C}$ for each $i=1,2,3.$ We can do this simultaneously by considering the following matrix:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14067114/assets/9d774b5bd79f14bc31e88a649fcb2a682d94ae3dd8acde5e25f52369c136e11e.png)

We reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 & 1 & -3 & 7 \\ 1 & -3 & 2 & -5 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:=(-1){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -1 & 3 & -7 \\ 1 & -3 & 2 & -5 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -1 & 3 & -7 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -8 & 8\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+4{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 11 & -29 & 25 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -8 & 8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the right-hand side gives the matrix of the linear transformation relative to the bases $\mathcal{B}$ and $\mathcal{C} \mathbin{:}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14067114/assets/778f179c4681bcdcc5a64bcd128d946a272fa869289d2c2e542df75ad05850b6.png)

e-5521.knowledge_point: Finding the Image of a Vector Under a Linear Map Given the Matrix Relative to Two Bases
e-5521.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14067114/assets/7d82125089d15dada1be4f8d6669b5e125da921019b3a9d27376353dcf59a090.png)

Suppose $\mathcal{B}$ and $\mathcal{C}$ are bases of the vector spaces $V$ and $W,$ respectively. The matrix $[\mathbf{T}]_{\mathcal{B}|\mathcal{C}}$ of the linear map $\mathbf{T}:V \rightarrow W$ relative to these bases, and the coordinates of the vector $\mathbf{x} \in V$ relative to $\mathcal{B}$ are shown above. Find $[\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{x})]_{\mathcal{C}}.$
e-5521.worked_solution:
The coordinates of the image of $\mathbf{x}$ under $\mathbf{T}$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{C}$ can be found as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[T(x)]_{C} & =[T]_{B|C}\cdot [x]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -2 \\ 3 & 7 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

e-5522.knowledge_point: Finding the Image of a Vector Given With Respect to the Standard Basis Under a Linear Map
e-5522.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14067114/assets/8caf13cdbf21ddfb1a121ede6ec0c21da155065905547bbd86b0e52cd57141da.png)

Consider the basis $\mathcal{B}$ of $\mathbb{R}^2$ (shown above) and a basis $\mathcal{C}$ of $\mathbb{R}^3.$
The matrix $[\mathbf{T}]_{\mathcal{B}|\mathcal{C}}$ of the linear map $\mathbf{T}:\mathbb{R}^2 \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^3$ relative to these bases, and the vector $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^2,$ are also given. Find $[\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{x})]_{\mathcal{C}}.$
e-5522.worked_solution:
We can find the coordinates of the image of $\mathbf{x}$ under $\mathbf{T}$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{C}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[T(x)]_{C} & =[T]_{B|C}\cdot [x]_{B}\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to find $[\mathbf{x}]_{\mathcal{B}},$ the coordinates of $\mathbf{x}$ relative to $\mathcal{B}.$ So, let

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14067114/assets/a5b6f5f41dffd99a885bb872eac6f1e6a24bd604b360256194a0bf16b32ef381.png)

This gives us the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=5 \\ 4{x}_{1}-5{x}_{2}=2.\end{aligned}
$$

We now row-reduce the corresponding augmented matrix using Gaussian elimination, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 5 \\ 4 & -5 & 2\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-4){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 5 \\ 0 & 3 & -18\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -6\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+2{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -7 \\ 0 & 1 & -6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14067114/assets/862742d57ad0ae4b56d6f345d825313bebf0d712f9c59ea1ed8b55d0a2eea22e.png)

Finally, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}[T(x)]_{C} & =[T]_{B|C}\cdot [x]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 \\ 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}17 \\ -9 \\ -6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 1
?

Suppose T:V→W is a linear map and B={b1,b2,b3} and C={c1,c2} are the bases of the vector spaces V and W, respectively. Find the matrix [T]B|C of the map T relative to these bases, if [T(b1)]C=[−48],[T(b2)]C=[6−1],[T(b3)]C=[8−3].

a
[T]B|C=[86−4−3−18]
b
[T]B|C=[46−3−8−18]
c
[T]B|C=[8−3−16−48]
d
[T]B|C=[−486−18−3]
e
[T]B|C=[−4688−1−3]
Submit

decision.explanation: The columns are the C-coordinate vectors of T(b₁), T(b₂), and T(b₃), in that order. Thus the rows are (-4, 6, 8) and (8, -1, -3), matching option e.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Suppose $T:V\to W$ is a linear map and $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}$ and $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2}}$ are the bases of the vector spaces $V$ and $W$, respectively. Find the matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the map $T$ relative to these bases, if 

$$
[T({b}_{1})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 8\end{aligned}],\,[T({b}_{2})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,[T({b}_{3})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that $[T]_{B|C}$ is the matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1}),$ $T({b}_{2}),$ and $T({b}_{3})$ relative to the basis $C.$ Therefore,

$$
[\begin{aligned}-4 & 6 & 8 \\ 8 & -1 & -3\end{aligned}].
$$

after.html:
Question 1
?

Suppose T:V→W is a linear map and B={b1,b2,b3} and C={c1,c2} are the bases of the vector spaces V and W, respectively. Find the matrix [T]B|C of the map T relative to these bases, if [T(b1)]C=[−48],[T(b2)]C=[6−1],[T(b3)]C=[8−3].

a
[T]B|C=[86−4−3−18]
b
[T]B|C=[46−3−8−18]
c
[T]B|C=[8−3−16−48]
d
[T]B|C=[−486−18−3]
e
[T]B|C=[−4688−1−3]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that [T]B|C is the matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors T(b1), T(b2), and T(b3) relative to the basis C. Therefore, [−4688−1−3].

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Matrix of a Linear Map Relative to Two Bases Using the Definition
content.problem:
Suppose $T:V\to W$ is a linear map and $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}$ and $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2}}$ are the bases of the vector spaces $V$ and $W$, respectively. Find the matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the map $T$ relative to these bases, if 

$$
[T({b}_{1})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 8\end{aligned}],\,[T({b}_{2})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,[T({b}_{3})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that $[T]_{B|C}$ is the matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1}),$ $T({b}_{2}),$ and $T({b}_{3})$ relative to the basis $C.$ Therefore,

$$
[\begin{aligned}-4 & 6 & 8 \\ 8 & -1 & -3\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 2
?

Suppose T:V→W is a linear map and B={b1,b2} and C={c1,c2,c3} are the bases of the vector spaces V and W, respectively. Find the matrix [T]B|C of the map T relative to these bases, if

T(b1)=c1−c2+c3 and T(b2)=2c2−c3.

a
[T]B|C=[−121−110]
b
[T]B|C=[1−1102−1]
c
[T]B|C=[10−121−1]
d
[T]B|C=[012−11−1]
e
[T]B|C=[02−11−11]
Submit

decision.explanation: The columns are the coordinates of T(b₁) and T(b₂) relative to C: (1, -1, 1) and (0, 2, -1). This gives option c.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Suppose $T:V\to W$ is a linear map and $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}$ and $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2},{c}_{3}}$ are the bases of the vector spaces $V$ and $W$, respectively. Find the matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the map $T$ relative to these bases, if 

$\,$ $T({b}_{1})={c}_{1}-{c}_{2}+{c}_{3}\,$ and $\,T({b}_{2})=2{c}_{2}-{c}_{3}.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we write the images of vectors in $B$ relative to the basis $C:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}T({b}_{1})={c}_{1}-{c}_{2}+{c}_{3} & \,⟹\,[T({b}_{1})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T({b}_{2})=2{c}_{2}-{c}_{3} & \,⟹\,[T({b}_{2})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, $[T]_{B|C}$ is the matrix  whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1})$ and  $T({b}_{2})$ relative to the basis $C:$

$$
[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 2 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

Question 2
?

Suppose T:V→W is a linear map and B={b1,b2} and C={c1,c2,c3} are the bases of the vector spaces V and W, respectively. Find the matrix [T]B|C of the map T relative to these bases, if

T(b1)=c1−c2+c3 and T(b2)=2c2−c3.

a
[T]B|C=[−121−110]
b
[T]B|C=[1−1102−1]
c
[T]B|C=[10−121−1]
d
[T]B|C=[012−11−1]
e
[T]B|C=[02−11−11]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we write the images of vectors in B relative to the basis C:

T(b1)=c1−c2+c3⟹[T(b1)]C=[1−11]T(b2)=2c2−c3⟹[T(b2)]C=[02−1]

Now, [T]B|C is the matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors T(b1) and T(b2) relative to the basis C: [T]B|C=[10−121−1]

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms that the coordinate vectors (1, -1, 1) and (0, 2, -1) form the columns, giving option c. Option b places them in rows instead.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Matrix of a Linear Map Relative to Two Bases Using the Definition
content.problem:
Suppose $T:V\to W$ is a linear map and $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}$ and $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2},{c}_{3}}$ are the bases of the vector spaces $V$ and $W$, respectively. Find the matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the map $T$ relative to these bases, if 

$\,$ $T({b}_{1})={c}_{1}-{c}_{2}+{c}_{3}\,$ and $\,T({b}_{2})=2{c}_{2}-{c}_{3}.$
content.worked_solution:
First, we write the images of vectors in $B$ relative to the basis $C:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}T({b}_{1})={c}_{1}-{c}_{2}+{c}_{3} & \,⟹\,[T({b}_{1})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T({b}_{2})=2{c}_{2}-{c}_{3} & \,⟹\,[T({b}_{2})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, $[T]_{B|C}$ is the matrix  whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1})$ and  $T({b}_{2})$ relative to the basis $C:$

$$
[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 2 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

Question 3
?

Suppose T:V→W is a linear map and B={b1,b2,b3} and C={c1,c2} are the bases of the vector spaces V and W, respectively. Find the matrix [T]B|C of the map T relative to these bases, if

[T(b1)]C=[−27],[T(b2)]C=[0−5],[T(b3)]C=[14].

a
[T]B|C=[71−504−2]
b
[T]B|C=[−25−13−54]
c
[T]B|C=[4077−6−2]
d
[T]B|C=[2−51−10−2]
e
[T]B|C=[−2017−54]
Submit

decision.explanation: Place the given C-coordinate vectors in columns in the order b₁, b₂, b₃. The resulting rows are (-2, 0, 1) and (7, -5, 4), matching option e.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Suppose $T:V\to W$ is a linear map and $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}$ and $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2}}$ are the bases of the vector spaces $V$ and $W$, respectively. Find the matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the map $T$ relative to these bases, if 

$$
[T({b}_{1})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 7\end{aligned}],\,[T({b}_{2})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -5\end{aligned}],\,[T({b}_{3})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that $[T]_{B|C}$ is the matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1}),$ $T({b}_{2}),$ and $T({b}_{3})$ relative to the basis $C.$ Therefore,

$$
[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & 1 \\ 7 & -5 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Suppose T:V→W is a linear map and B={b1,b2,b3} and C={c1,c2} are the bases of the vector spaces V and W, respectively. Find the matrix [T]B|C of the map T relative to these bases, if

[T(b1)]C=[−27],[T(b2)]C=[0−5],[T(b3)]C=[14].

a
[T]B|C=[71−504−2]
b
[T]B|C=[−25−13−54]
c
[T]B|C=[4077−6−2]
d
[T]B|C=[2−51−10−2]
e
[T]B|C=[−2017−54]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that [T]B|C is the matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors T(b1), T(b2), and T(b3) relative to the basis C. Therefore,

[T]B|C=[−2017−54].

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Matrix of a Linear Map Relative to Two Bases Using the Definition
content.problem:
Suppose $T:V\to W$ is a linear map and $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}$ and $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2}}$ are the bases of the vector spaces $V$ and $W$, respectively. Find the matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the map $T$ relative to these bases, if 

$$
[T({b}_{1})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 7\end{aligned}],\,[T({b}_{2})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -5\end{aligned}],\,[T({b}_{3})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that $[T]_{B|C}$ is the matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1}),$ $T({b}_{2}),$ and $T({b}_{3})$ relative to the basis $C.$ Therefore,

$$
[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & 1 \\ 7 & -5 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

before.html:
Question 4
?

Suppose T:V→W is a linear map and B={b1,b2} and C={c1,c2,c3} are the bases of the vector spaces V and W, respectively. Find the matrix [T]B|C of the map T relative to these bases, if

T(b1)=−2c1+4c2−2c3 and T(b2)=3c2−7c3+c1.

a
[T]B|C=[14−7−23−2]
b
[T]B|C=[1−234−7−2]
c
[T]B|C=[−2143−2−7]
d
[T]B|C=[−24−213−7]
e
[T]B|C=[1−243−2−7]
Submit

decision.explanation: The C-coordinate vectors of T(b₁) and T(b₂) are (-2, 4, -2) and (1, 3, -7). Placing them as the first and second columns gives option c.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
Suppose $T:V\to W$ is a linear map and $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}$ and $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2},{c}_{3}}$ are the bases of the vector spaces $V$ and $W$, respectively. Find the matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the map $T$ relative to these bases, if 

$\,$ $T({b}_{1})=-2{c}_{1}+4{c}_{2}-2{c}_{3}\,$ and $\,T({b}_{2})=3{c}_{2}-7{c}_{3}+{c}_{1}.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we write the images of vectors in $B$ relative to the basis $C:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}T({b}_{1})=-2{c}_{1}+4{c}_{2}-2{c}_{3} & \,⟹\,[T({b}_{1})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\ T({b}_{2})=3{c}_{2}-7{c}_{3}+{c}_{1} & \,⟹\,[T({b}_{2})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ -7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, $[T]_{B|C}$ is the matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1})$ and  $T({b}_{2})$ relative to the basis $C:$

$$
[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 4 & 3 \\ -2 & -7\end{aligned}]
$$

Question 4
?

Suppose T:V→W is a linear map and B={b1,b2} and C={c1,c2,c3} are the bases of the vector spaces V and W, respectively. Find the matrix [T]B|C of the map T relative to these bases, if

T(b1)=−2c1+4c2−2c3 and T(b2)=3c2−7c3+c1.

a
[T]B|C=[14−7−23−2]
b
[T]B|C=[1−234−7−2]
c
[T]B|C=[−2143−2−7]
d
[T]B|C=[−24−213−7]
e
[T]B|C=[1−243−2−7]
Submit
Incorrect

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Matrix of a Linear Map Relative to Two Bases Using the Definition
content.problem:
Suppose $T:V\to W$ is a linear map and $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}$ and $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2},{c}_{3}}$ are the bases of the vector spaces $V$ and $W$, respectively. Find the matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the map $T$ relative to these bases, if 

$\,$ $T({b}_{1})=-2{c}_{1}+4{c}_{2}-2{c}_{3}\,$ and $\,T({b}_{2})=3{c}_{2}-7{c}_{3}+{c}_{1}.$
content.worked_solution:
First, we write the images of vectors in $B$ relative to the basis $C:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}T({b}_{1})=-2{c}_{1}+4{c}_{2}-2{c}_{3} & \,⟹\,[T({b}_{1})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\ T({b}_{2})=3{c}_{2}-7{c}_{3}+{c}_{1} & \,⟹\,[T({b}_{2})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ -7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, $[T]_{B|C}$ is the matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1})$ and  $T({b}_{2})$ relative to the basis $C:$

$$
[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 4 & 3 \\ -2 & -7\end{aligned}]
$$

Question 5
?

Suppose T:V→W is a linear map and B={b1,b2,b3} and C={c1,c2} are the bases of the vector spaces V and W, respectively. Find the matrix [T]B|C of the map T relative to these bases, if

[T(b1)]C=[6−5],[T(b2)]C=[47],[T(b3)]C=[0−2].

a
[T]B|C=[6−5470−2]
b
[T]B|C=[7−2−5406]
c
[T]B|C=[640−57−2]
d
[T]B|C=[−5647−20]
e
[T]B|C=[−57064−2]
Submit

decision.explanation: The matrix has the given C-coordinate vectors as columns, in order: (6, -5), (4, 7), and (0, -2). This matches option c.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
Suppose $T:V\to W$ is a linear map and $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}$ and $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2}}$ are the bases of the vector spaces $V$ and $W$, respectively. Find the matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the map $T$ relative to these bases, if 

$$
[T({b}_{1})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -5\end{aligned}],\,[T({b}_{2})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 7\end{aligned}],\,[T({b}_{3})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that $[T]_{B|C}$ is the matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1}),$ $T({b}_{2}),$ and $T({b}_{3})$ relative to the basis $C.$ Therefore,

$$
[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}6 & 4 & 0 \\ -5 & 7 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Suppose T:V→W is a linear map and B={b1,b2,b3} and C={c1,c2} are the bases of the vector spaces V and W, respectively. Find the matrix [T]B|C of the map T relative to these bases, if

[T(b1)]C=[6−5],[T(b2)]C=[47],[T(b3)]C=[0−2].

a
[T]B|C=[6−5470−2]
b
[T]B|C=[7−2−5406]
c
[T]B|C=[640−57−2]
d
[T]B|C=[−5647−20]
e
[T]B|C=[−57064−2]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that [T]B|C is the matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors T(b1), T(b2), and T(b3) relative to the basis C. Therefore,

[T]B|C=[640−57−2].

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Matrix of a Linear Map Relative to Two Bases Using the Definition
content.problem:
Suppose $T:V\to W$ is a linear map and $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}$ and $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2}}$ are the bases of the vector spaces $V$ and $W$, respectively. Find the matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the map $T$ relative to these bases, if 

$$
[T({b}_{1})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -5\end{aligned}],\,[T({b}_{2})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 7\end{aligned}],\,[T({b}_{3})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that $[T]_{B|C}$ is the matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1}),$ $T({b}_{2}),$ and $T({b}_{3})$ relative to the basis $C.$ Therefore,

$$
[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}6 & 4 & 0 \\ -5 & 7 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

before.name: Question 6
before.problem:
Consider the basis $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}$ of the vector space $V$ and the basis $C$ of ${R}^{2}$ given by

$$
C={[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 6\end{aligned}]}.
$$

Find the matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the map $T:V\to {R}^{2}$ relative to these bases if 

$$
T({b}_{1})=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,T({b}_{2})=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

after.name: Question 6
after.problem:
Consider the basis $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}$ of the vector space $V$ and the basis $C$ of ${R}^{2}$ given by

$$
C={[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 6\end{aligned}]}.
$$

Find the matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the map $T:V\to {R}^{2}$ relative to these bases if 

$$
T({b}_{1})=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,T({b}_{2})=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that $[T]_{B|C}$ is the matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1})$ and $T({b}_{2})$ relative to the basis $C.$

First, we need to find the coordinates of $T({b}_{i})$ relative to the basis $C$ for each $i=1,2.$ We can do this simultaneously by considering the following matrix:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ {c}_{1} & {c}_{2} & T({b}_{1}) & T({b}_{2}) \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

We reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & -2 & -4 \\ 4 & 6 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 & -2 \\ 4 & 6 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-4){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & 6 & 12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -4 & -8 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the right-hand side gives the matrix of the linear transformation relative to the bases $B$ and $C:$

$$
[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}-4 & -8 \\ 3 & 6\end{aligned}]
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Matrix of a Linear Map Relative to Two Bases Given One Basis
content.problem:
Consider the basis $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}$ of the vector space $V$ and the basis $C$ of ${R}^{2}$ given by

$$
C={[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 6\end{aligned}]}.
$$

Find the matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the map $T:V\to {R}^{2}$ relative to these bases if 

$$
T({b}_{1})=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,T({b}_{2})=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that $[T]_{B|C}$ is the matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1})$ and $T({b}_{2})$ relative to the basis $C.$

First, we need to find the coordinates of $T({b}_{i})$ relative to the basis $C$ for each $i=1,2.$ We can do this simultaneously by considering the following matrix:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ {c}_{1} & {c}_{2} & T({b}_{1}) & T({b}_{2}) \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

We reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination:

$$

$$

Finally, the right-hand side gives the matrix of the linear transformation relative to the bases $B$ and $C:$

$$
[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}-4 & -8 \\ 3 & 6\end{aligned}]
$$

after.name: Question 7
after.problem:
Consider the basis $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}$ of the vector space $V$ and the basis $C$ of ${R}^{2}$ given by

$$
C={[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5\end{aligned}]}.
$$

Find the matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the map $T:V\to {R}^{2}$ relative to these bases if 

$$
T({b}_{1})=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 7\end{aligned}],\,T({b}_{2})=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that $[T]_{B|C}$ is the matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1})$ and $T({b}_{2})$ relative to the basis $C.$

First, we need to find the coordinates of $T({b}_{i})$ relative to the basis $C$ for each $i=1,2.$ We can do this simultaneously by considering the following matrix:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ {c}_{1} & {c}_{2} & T({b}_{1}) & T({b}_{2}) \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

We reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 5 & -2 \\ -2 & 5 & 7 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -5 & 2 \\ -2 & 5 & 7 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -5 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -11 & 12 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the right-hand side gives the matrix of the linear transformation relative to the bases $B$ and $C:$

$$
[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}-11 & 12 \\ -3 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

Question 7
?

Consider the basis B={b1,b2} of the vector space V and the basis C of R2 given by C={[−1−2],[25]}.

Find the matrix [T]B|C of the map T:V→R2 relative to these bases if T(b1)=[57],T(b2)=[−21].

a
[12−11−35]
b
[−11−3125]
c
[512−3−11]
d
[−1112−35]
e
[−11125−3]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that [T]B|C is the matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors T(b1) and T(b2) relative to the basis C.

First, we need to find the coordinates of T(bi) relative to the basis C for each i=1,2. We can do this simultaneously by considering the following matrix:

M=[||||c1c2T(b1)T(b2)||||].

We reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination:

M=[−125−2−2571]R1:=(−1)R1∼[1−2−52−2571]R2:=R2+2R1∼[1−2−5201−35]R1:=R1+2R2∼[10−111201−35]

Finally, the right-hand side gives the matrix of the linear transformation relative to the bases B and C:

[T]B|C=[−1112−35]

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Matrix of a Linear Map Relative to Two Bases Given One Basis
content.problem:
Consider the basis $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}$ of the vector space $V$ and the basis $C$ of ${R}^{2}$ given by

$$
C={[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5\end{aligned}]}.
$$

Find the matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the map $T:V\to {R}^{2}$ relative to these bases if 

$$
T({b}_{1})=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 7\end{aligned}],\,T({b}_{2})=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that $[T]_{B|C}$ is the matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1})$ and $T({b}_{2})$ relative to the basis $C.$

First, we need to find the coordinates of $T({b}_{i})$ relative to the basis $C$ for each $i=1,2.$ We can do this simultaneously by considering the following matrix:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ {c}_{1} & {c}_{2} & T({b}_{1}) & T({b}_{2}) \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

We reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 5 & -2 \\ -2 & 5 & 7 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -5 & 2 \\ -2 & 5 & 7 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -5 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -11 & 12 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the right-hand side gives the matrix of the linear transformation relative to the bases $B$ and $C:$

$$
[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}-11 & 12 \\ -3 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

before.problem:
Consider the basis $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}$ of the vector space $V$ and the basis $C$ of ${R}^{2}$ given by

$$
C={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5\end{aligned}]}.
$$

Find the matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the map $T:V\to {R}^{2}$ relative to these bases if 

$$
T({b}_{1})=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,T({b}_{2})=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,T({b}_{3})=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 8
?

Consider the basis B={b1,b2,b3} of the vector space V and the basis C of R2 given by C={[13],[05]}.

Find the matrix [T]B|C of the map T:V→R2 relative to these bases if T(b1)=[42],T(b2)=[−12],T(b3)=[−31].

a
[4−2−321−1]
b
[4−1−3−212]
c
[−3−11−242]
d
[−14−3−221]
e
[421−2−3−1]
Submit

decision.explanation: Relative to C, a vector (x,y) has coordinates (x,(y-3x)/5). The three images therefore have coordinates (4,-2), (-1,1), and (-3,2). Using these as columns gives option b.

after.name: Question 8
after.problem:
Consider the basis $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}$ of the vector space $V$ and the basis $C$ of ${R}^{2}$ given by

$$
C={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5\end{aligned}]}.
$$

Find the matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the map $T:V\to {R}^{2}$ relative to these bases if 

$$
T({b}_{1})=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,T({b}_{2})=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,T({b}_{3})=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that $[T]_{B|C}$ is the matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1}),$ $T({b}_{2}),$ and $T({b}_{3})$ relative to the basis $C.$

First, we need to find the coordinates of $T({b}_{i})$ relative to the basis $C$ for each $i=1,2,3.$ We can do this simultaneously by considering the following matrix:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | & | \\ {c}_{1} & {c}_{2} & T({b}_{1}) & T({b}_{2}) & T({b}_{3}) \\ | & | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

We reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 4 & -1 & -3 \\ 3 & 5 & 2 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 4 & -1 & -3 \\ 0 & 5 & -10 & 5 & 10\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 4 & -1 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the right-hand side gives the matrix of the linear transformation relative to the bases $B$ and $C:$

$$
[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 & -3 \\ -2 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Question 8
?

Consider the basis B={b1,b2,b3} of the vector space V and the basis C of R2 given by C={[13],[05]}.

Find the matrix [T]B|C of the map T:V→R2 relative to these bases if T(b1)=[42],T(b2)=[−12],T(b3)=[−31].

a
[4−2−321−1]
b
[4−1−3−212]
c
[−3−11−242]
d
[−14−3−221]
e
[421−2−3−1]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Recall that [T]B|C is the matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors T(b1), T(b2), and T(b3) relative to the basis C.

First, we need to find the coordinates of T(bi) relative to the basis C for each i=1,2,3. We can do this simultaneously by considering the following matrix:

M=[|||||c1c2T(b1)T(b2)T(b3)|||||].

We reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination:

M=[104−1−335221]R2:=R2+(−3)R1∼[104−1−305−10510]R2:=15R2∼[104−1−301−212]

Finally, the right-hand side gives the matrix of the linear transformation relative to the bases B and C:

[T]B|C=[4−1−3−212]

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms columns (4,-2), (-1,1), and (-3,2). Indeed, 4c₁−2c₂=(4,2), −c₁+c₂=(-1,2), and −3c₁+2c₂=(-3,1). Thus option b is correct.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Matrix of a Linear Map Relative to Two Bases Given One Basis
content.problem:
Consider the basis $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}$ of the vector space $V$ and the basis $C$ of ${R}^{2}$ given by

$$
C={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5\end{aligned}]}.
$$

Find the matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the map $T:V\to {R}^{2}$ relative to these bases if 

$$
T({b}_{1})=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,T({b}_{2})=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,T({b}_{3})=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that $[T]_{B|C}$ is the matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1}),$ $T({b}_{2}),$ and $T({b}_{3})$ relative to the basis $C.$

First, we need to find the coordinates of $T({b}_{i})$ relative to the basis $C$ for each $i=1,2,3.$ We can do this simultaneously by considering the following matrix:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | & | \\ {c}_{1} & {c}_{2} & T({b}_{1}) & T({b}_{2}) & T({b}_{3}) \\ | & | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

We reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 4 & -1 & -3 \\ 3 & 5 & 2 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 4 & -1 & -3 \\ 0 & 5 & -10 & 5 & 10\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 4 & -1 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the right-hand side gives the matrix of the linear transformation relative to the bases $B$ and $C:$

$$
[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 & -3 \\ -2 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Question 9
?

Consider the basis B={b1,b2,b3} of the vector space V and the basis C of R2 given by C={[1−3],[3−8]}.

Find the matrix [T]B|C of the map T:V→R2 relative to these bases if T(b1)=[−22],T(b2)=[14],T(b3)=[−3−1].

a
[10727−10−20−4]
b
[10−2027−47−10]
c
[7−1042810−20]
d
[10−4−10−20727]
e
[7−20−42710−10]
Submit

decision.explanation: With c₁=(1,-3) and c₂=(3,-8), 10c₁−4c₂=(-2,2), −20c₁+7c₂=(1,4), and 27c₁−10c₂=(-3,-1). These coefficients form the columns, matching option b.

after.name: Question 9
after.problem:
Consider the basis $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}$ of the vector space $V$ and the basis $C$ of ${R}^{2}$ given by

$$
C={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -8\end{aligned}]}.
$$

Find the matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the map $T:V\to {R}^{2}$ relative to these bases if 

$$
T({b}_{1})=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,T({b}_{2})=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4\end{aligned}],\,T({b}_{3})=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that $[T]_{B|C}$ is the matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1}),$ $T({b}_{2}),$ and $T({b}_{3})$ relative to the basis $C.$

First, we need to find the coordinates of $T({b}_{i})$ relative to the basis $C$ for each $i=1,2,3.$ We can do this simultaneously by considering the following matrix:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | & | \\ {c}_{1} & {c}_{2} & T({b}_{1}) & T({b}_{2}) & T({b}_{3}) \\ | & | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

We reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -2 & 1 & -3 \\ -3 & -8 & 2 & 4 & -1\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -2 & 1 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & 7 & -10\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-3){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 10 & -20 & 27 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & 7 & -10\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the right-hand side gives the matrix of the linear transformation relative to the bases $B$ and $C:$

$$
[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}10 & -20 & 27 \\ -4 & 7 & -10\end{aligned}]
$$

Question 9

Consider the basis B={b1,b2,b3} of the vector space V and the basis C of R2 given by C={[1−3],[3−8]}.

Find the matrix [T]B|C of the map T:V→R2 relative to these bases if T(b1)=[−22],T(b2)=[14],T(b3)=[−3−1].

a
[10727−10−20−4]
b
[10−2027−47−10]
c
[7−1042810−20]
d
[10−4−10−20727]
e
[7−20−42710−10]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that [T]B|C is the matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors T(b1), T(b2), and T(b3) relative to the basis C.

First, we need to find the coordinates of T(bi) relative to the basis C for each i=1,2,3. We can do this simultaneously by considering the following matrix:

M=[|||||c1c2T(b1)T(b2)T(b3)|||||].

We reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination:

M=[13−21−3−3−824−1]R2:=R2+3R1∼[13−21−301−47−10]R1:=R1+(−3)R2∼[1010−202701−47−10]

Finally, the right-hand side gives the matrix of the linear transformation relative to the bases B and C:

[T]B|C=[10−2027−47−10]

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Matrix of a Linear Map Relative to Two Bases Given One Basis
content.problem:
Consider the basis $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}$ of the vector space $V$ and the basis $C$ of ${R}^{2}$ given by

$$
C={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -8\end{aligned}]}.
$$

Find the matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the map $T:V\to {R}^{2}$ relative to these bases if 

$$
T({b}_{1})=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,T({b}_{2})=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4\end{aligned}],\,T({b}_{3})=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that $[T]_{B|C}$ is the matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1}),$ $T({b}_{2}),$ and $T({b}_{3})$ relative to the basis $C.$

First, we need to find the coordinates of $T({b}_{i})$ relative to the basis $C$ for each $i=1,2,3.$ We can do this simultaneously by considering the following matrix:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | & | \\ {c}_{1} & {c}_{2} & T({b}_{1}) & T({b}_{2}) & T({b}_{3}) \\ | & | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

We reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -2 & 1 & -3 \\ -3 & -8 & 2 & 4 & -1\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -2 & 1 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & 7 & -10\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-3){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 10 & -20 & 27 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & 7 & -10\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the right-hand side gives the matrix of the linear transformation relative to the bases $B$ and $C:$

$$
[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}10 & -20 & 27 \\ -4 & 7 & -10\end{aligned}]
$$

after.name: Question 10
after.problem:
Consider the basis $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}$ of the vector space $V$ and the basis $C$ of ${R}^{2}$ given by

$$
C={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]}.
$$

Find the matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the map $T:V\to {R}^{2}$ relative to these bases if 

$$
T({b}_{1})=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,T({b}_{2})=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,T({b}_{3})=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that $[T]_{B|C}$ is the matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1}),$ $T({b}_{2}),$ and $T({b}_{3})$ relative to the basis $C.$

First, we need to find the coordinates of $T({b}_{i})$ relative to the basis $C$ for each $i=1,2,3.$ We can do this simultaneously by considering the following matrix:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | & | \\ {c}_{1} & {c}_{2} & T({b}_{1}) & T({b}_{2}) & T({b}_{3}) \\ | & | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

We reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 & -1 & 1 \\ 3 & 4 & 1 & -1 & -3\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & -8 & 2 & -6\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:=(-\frac{1}{2}){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -5 & 1 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the right-hand side gives the matrix of the linear transformation relative to the bases $B$ and $C:$

$$
[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}-5 & 1 & -5 \\ 4 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

after.name: Question 11
after.problem:
$$
[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}9 & -2 \\ 1 & -3 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}],\,[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4\end{aligned}]
$$

Suppose $B$ and $C$ are bases of the vector spaces $V$ and $W,$ respectively. The matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the linear map $T:V\to W$ relative to these bases, and the coordinates of the vector $x\in V$ relative to $B$ are shown above. Find $[T(x)]_{C}.$
after.worked_solution:
The coordinates of the image of $x$ under $T$ relative to the basis $C$ can be found as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[T(x)]_{C} & =[T]_{B|C}\cdot [x]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}9 & -2 \\ 1 & -3 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -11 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Image of a Vector Under a Linear Map Given the Matrix Relative to Two Bases
content.problem:
$$
[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}9 & -2 \\ 1 & -3 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}],\,[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4\end{aligned}]
$$

Suppose $B$ and $C$ are bases of the vector spaces $V$ and $W,$ respectively. The matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the linear map $T:V\to W$ relative to these bases, and the coordinates of the vector $x\in V$ relative to $B$ are shown above. Find $[T(x)]_{C}.$
content.worked_solution:
The coordinates of the image of $x$ under $T$ relative to the basis $C$ can be found as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[T(x)]_{C} & =[T]_{B|C}\cdot [x]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}9 & -2 \\ 1 & -3 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -11 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms the matrix product: 5(-5)−4+7=−22 and (−2)(−5)+12+4=26. Thus option a is correct.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Image of a Vector Under a Linear Map Given the Matrix Relative to Two Bases
content.problem:
$$
[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}5 & -1 & -7 \\ -2 & 3 & -4\end{aligned}],\,[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 4 \\ -1\end{aligned}]
$$

Suppose $B$ and $C$ are bases of the vector spaces $V$ and $W,$ respectively. The matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the linear map $T:V\to W$ relative to these bases, and the coordinates of the vector $x\in V$ relative to $B$ are shown above. Find $[T(x)]_{C}.$
content.worked_solution:
The coordinates of the image of $x$ under $T$ relative to the basis $C$ can be found as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[T(x)]_{C} & =[T]_{B|C}\cdot [x]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & -1 & -7 \\ -2 & 3 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 4 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-22 \\ 26\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Multiply [T]_{B|C} by [x]_B: (−5)(−3)+2=17, 8(−3)+0=−24, and 7(−3)−4=−25. This matches option e.

after.name: Question 14
after.problem:
$$
[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}-5 & 2 \\ 8 & 0 \\ 7 & -4\end{aligned}],\,[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Suppose $B$ and $C$ are bases of the vector spaces $V$ and $W,$ respectively. The matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the linear map $T:V\to W$ relative to these bases, and the coordinates of the vector $x\in V$ relative to $B$ are shown above. Find $[T(x)]_{C}.$
after.worked_solution:
The coordinates of the image of $x$ under $T$ relative to the basis $C$ can be found as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[T(x)]_{C} & =[T]_{B|C}\cdot [x]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & 2 \\ 8 & 0 \\ 7 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}17 \\ -24 \\ -25\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Image of a Vector Under a Linear Map Given the Matrix Relative to Two Bases
content.problem:
$$
[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}-5 & 2 \\ 8 & 0 \\ 7 & -4\end{aligned}],\,[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Suppose $B$ and $C$ are bases of the vector spaces $V$ and $W,$ respectively. The matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the linear map $T:V\to W$ relative to these bases, and the coordinates of the vector $x\in V$ relative to $B$ are shown above. Find $[T(x)]_{C}.$
content.worked_solution:
The coordinates of the image of $x$ under $T$ relative to the basis $C$ can be found as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[T(x)]_{C} & =[T]_{B|C}\cdot [x]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & 2 \\ 8 & 0 \\ 7 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}17 \\ -24 \\ -25\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

$$

B={[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5\end{aligned}]},\,[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 3 & -2\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -3\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the basis $B$ of ${R}^{2}$ (shown above) and a basis $C$ of ${R}^{3}.$
The matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the linear map $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{3}$ relative to these bases, and the vector $x\in {R}^{2},$ are also given. Find $[T(x)]_{C}.$
after.worked_solution:
We can find the coordinates of the image of $x$ under $T$ relative to the basis $C$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[T(x)]_{C} & =[T]_{B|C}\cdot [x]_{B}\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to find $[x]_{B},$ the coordinates of $x$ relative to $B.$ So, let

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -3\end{aligned}]={x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5\end{aligned}].
$$

This gives us the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}=-4 \\ -2{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}=-3.\end{aligned}
$$

We now row-reduce the corresponding augmented matrix using Gaussian elimination, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & -4 \\ -2 & 5 & -3\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:=(-1){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 4 \\ -2 & 5 & -3\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 5 & 5\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

Finally, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}[T(x)]_{C} & =[T]_{B|C}\cdot [x]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 3 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 5 \\ 10\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

$$

after.name: Question 17
after.problem:
$$
B={[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -5\end{aligned}]},\,[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 1 & -2 \\ -4 & 9\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the basis $B$ of ${R}^{2}$ (shown above) and a basis $C$ of ${R}^{3}.$
The matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the linear map $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{3}$ relative to these bases, and the vector $x\in {R}^{2},$ are also given. Find $[T(x)]_{C}.$
after.worked_solution:
We can find the coordinates of the image of $x$ under $T$ relative to the basis $C$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[T(x)]_{C} & =[T]_{B|C}\cdot [x]_{B}\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to find $[x]_{B},$ the coordinates of $x$ relative to $B.$ So, let

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]={x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -5\end{aligned}].
$$

This gives us the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=2 \\ 2{x}_{1}-5{x}_{2}=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

We now row-reduce the corresponding augmented matrix using Gaussian elimination, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 & 2 \\ 2 & -5 & -1\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:=(-1){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -2 \\ 2 & -5 & -1\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+3{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 7 \\ 0 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$

Finally, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}[T(x)]_{C} & =[T]_{B|C}\cdot [x]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 1 & -2 \\ -4 & 9\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}7 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}16 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Image of a Vector Given With Respect to the Standard Basis Under a Linear Map
content.problem:
$$
B={[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -5\end{aligned}]},\,[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 1 & -2 \\ -4 & 9\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the basis $B$ of ${R}^{2}$ (shown above) and a basis $C$ of ${R}^{3}.$
The matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the linear map $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{3}$ relative to these bases, and the vector $x\in {R}^{2},$ are also given. Find $[T(x)]_{C}.$
content.worked_solution:
We can find the coordinates of the image of $x$ under $T$ relative to the basis $C$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[T(x)]_{C} & =[T]_{B|C}\cdot [x]_{B}\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to find $[x]_{B},$ the coordinates of $x$ relative to $B.$ So, let

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]={x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -5\end{aligned}].
$$

This gives us the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=2 \\ 2{x}_{1}-5{x}_{2}=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

We now row-reduce the corresponding augmented matrix using Gaussian elimination, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 & 2 \\ 2 & -5 & -1\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:=(-1){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -2 \\ 2 & -5 & -1\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+3{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 7 \\ 0 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$

Finally, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}[T(x)]_{C} & =[T]_{B|C}\cdot [x]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 1 & -2 \\ -4 & 9\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}7 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}16 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem:
$$
B={[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 3\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}9 \\ -6\end{aligned}]},\,[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 \\ 4 & 0 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}-15 \\ 30\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the basis $B$ of ${R}^{2}$ (shown above) and a basis $C$ of ${R}^{3}.$
The matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the linear map $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{3}$ relative to these bases, and the vector $x\in {R}^{2},$ are also given. Find $[T(x)]_{C}.$
after.worked_solution:
We can find the coordinates of the image of $x$ under $T$ relative to the basis $C$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[T(x)]_{C} & =[T]_{B|C}\cdot [x]_{B}\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to find $[x]_{B},$ the coordinates of $x$ relative to $B.$ So, let

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}-15 \\ 30\end{aligned}]={x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}9 \\ -6\end{aligned}].
$$

This gives us the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{1}+9{x}_{2}=-15 \\ 3{x}_{1}-6{x}_{2}=30.\end{aligned}
$$

We now row-reduce the corresponding augmented matrix using Gaussian elimination, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 9 & -15 \\ 3 & -6 & 30\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:=(-\frac{1}{3}){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 5 \\ 3 & -6 & 30\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 5 \\ 0 & 3 & 15\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+3{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 20 \\ 0 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}20 \\ 5\end{aligned}].$

Finally, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}[T(x)]_{C} & =[T]_{B|C}\cdot [x]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 \\ 4 & 0 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}20 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}15 \\ 80 \\ -5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Image of a Vector Given With Respect to the Standard Basis Under a Linear Map
content.problem:
$$
B={[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 3\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}9 \\ -6\end{aligned}]},\,[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 \\ 4 & 0 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}-15 \\ 30\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the basis $B$ of ${R}^{2}$ (shown above) and a basis $C$ of ${R}^{3}.$
The matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the linear map $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{3}$ relative to these bases, and the vector $x\in {R}^{2},$ are also given. Find $[T(x)]_{C}.$
content.worked_solution:
We can find the coordinates of the image of $x$ under $T$ relative to the basis $C$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[T(x)]_{C} & =[T]_{B|C}\cdot [x]_{B}\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to find $[x]_{B},$ the coordinates of $x$ relative to $B.$ So, let

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}-15 \\ 30\end{aligned}]={x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}9 \\ -6\end{aligned}].
$$

This gives us the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{1}+9{x}_{2}=-15 \\ 3{x}_{1}-6{x}_{2}=30.\end{aligned}
$$

We now row-reduce the corresponding augmented matrix using Gaussian elimination, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 9 & -15 \\ 3 & -6 & 30\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:=(-\frac{1}{3}){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 5 \\ 3 & -6 & 30\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 5 \\ 0 & 3 & 15\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+3{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 20 \\ 0 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}20 \\ 5\end{aligned}].$

Finally, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}[T(x)]_{C} & =[T]_{B|C}\cdot [x]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 \\ 4 & 0 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}20 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}15 \\ 80 \\ -5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}[T(x)]_{C} & =[T]_{B|C}\cdot [x]_{B}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -5\end{aligned}]={x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 7\end{aligned}].
$$

This gives us the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=3 \\ 3{x}_{1}+7{x}_{2}=-5.\end{aligned}
$$

We now row-reduce the corresponding augmented matrix using Gaussian elimination, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & 3 \\ 3 & 7 & -5\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:=(-1){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3 \\ 3 & 7 & -5\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -11 \\ 0 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}[T(x)]_{C} & =[T]_{B|C}\cdot [x]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 7 \\ 3 & 8 \\ 2 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-11 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Image of a Vector Given With Respect to the Standard Basis Under a Linear Map
content.problem:
$$
B={[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 7\end{aligned}]},\,[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}3 & 7 \\ 3 & 8 \\ 2 & 6\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -5\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the basis $B$ of ${R}^{2}$ (shown above) and a basis $C$ of ${R}^{3}.$
The matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the linear map $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{3}$ relative to these bases, and the vector $x\in {R}^{2},$ are also given. Find $[T(x)]_{C}.$
content.worked_solution:
We can find the coordinates of the image of $x$ under $T$ relative to the basis $C$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[T(x)]_{C} & =[T]_{B|C}\cdot [x]_{B}\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to find $[x]_{B},$ the coordinates of $x$ relative to $B.$ So, let

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -5\end{aligned}]={x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 7\end{aligned}].
$$

This gives us the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=3 \\ 3{x}_{1}+7{x}_{2}=-5.\end{aligned}
$$

We now row-reduce the corresponding augmented matrix using Gaussian elimination, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & 3 \\ 3 & 7 & -5\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:=(-1){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3 \\ 3 & 7 & -5\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -11 \\ 0 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-11 \\ 4\end{aligned}].$

Finally, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}[T(x)]_{C} & =[T]_{B|C}\cdot [x]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 7 \\ 3 & 8 \\ 2 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-11 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 20
after.problem:
$$
B={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -7\end{aligned}]},\,[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 4 & 6\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 6\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the basis $B$ of ${R}^{2}$ (shown above) and a basis $C$ of ${R}^{3}.$
The matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the linear map $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{3}$ relative to these bases, and the vector $x\in {R}^{2},$ are also given. Find $[T(x)]_{C}.$
after.worked_solution:
We can find the coordinates of the image of $x$ under $T$ relative to the basis $C$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[T(x)]_{C} & =[T]_{B|C}\cdot [x]_{B}\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to find $[x]_{B},$ the coordinates of $x$ relative to $B.$ So, let

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 6\end{aligned}]={x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -7\end{aligned}].
$$

This gives us the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=-1 \\ -4{x}_{1}-7{x}_{2}=6.\end{aligned}
$$

We now row-reduce the corresponding augmented matrix using Gaussian elimination, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ -4 & -7 & 6\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

Finally, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}[T(x)]_{C} & =[T]_{B|C}\cdot [x]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 4 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-11 \\ -3 \\ -8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Image of a Vector Given With Respect to the Standard Basis Under a Linear Map
content.problem:
$$
B={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -7\end{aligned}]},\,[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 4 & 6\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 6\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the basis $B$ of ${R}^{2}$ (shown above) and a basis $C$ of ${R}^{3}.$
The matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the linear map $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{3}$ relative to these bases, and the vector $x\in {R}^{2},$ are also given. Find $[T(x)]_{C}.$
content.worked_solution:
We can find the coordinates of the image of $x$ under $T$ relative to the basis $C$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[T(x)]_{C} & =[T]_{B|C}\cdot [x]_{B}\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to find $[x]_{B},$ the coordinates of $x$ relative to $B.$ So, let

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 6\end{aligned}]={x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -7\end{aligned}].
$$

This gives us the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=-1 \\ -4{x}_{1}-7{x}_{2}=6.\end{aligned}
$$

We now row-reduce the corresponding augmented matrix using Gaussian elimination, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ -4 & -7 & 6\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

Finally, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}[T(x)]_{C} & =[T]_{B|C}\cdot [x]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 4 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-11 \\ -3 \\ -8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
